image_prompt.text: Vehicle-width asphalt roads laid out as a street grid with four-way intersections, dividing the city into regular blocks
A dense city block grid, the blocks between the roads filled with buildings of varying height — some tall, some medium, some short — in browns, greys and blues
Grey sidewalks running along both edges of every road
Painted road markings — lane dividers down each street and crosswalks across every intersection
Street lights standing at the intersections, spaced evenly along the grid
Trees and small green vegetation planted along some of the sidewalks
Parking lots and open paved spaces occupying some of the city blocks

notes: Racing was the first candidate — "car game", "driving map" — but Racing's own boundary note is explicit that with no lap and no finish condition it is a vehicle sim, so Simulation leads and Racing is not named. This also keeps Racing's genre-wide P6 off a free-roam street grid that has no route to validate.

Preset Vehicle Sim taken with its own shape world-shared; its resource-shared option was dropped because a city driving map has no shared extraction field. Nothing else was changed, so the preset name stands.
settlement-density is a Universal Option and is used only because the prompt directly describes a dense grid of city blocks with varying-height buildings; it was not applied as a default.
Buildings are treated as street-facing facades — nothing in the prompt goes indoors — so building-interior and its P3 were deliberately not taken.

Sidewalks, lane markings and crosswalks, street lights, roadside trees and parking lots match no option in the loaded file, so they are carried as id: null image entries in the prompt's own words rather than dropped.

The requested configurable attributes (blockSize, roadWidth, gridCount, buildingHeightMin, buildingHeightMax, treeDensity, streetLightSpacing) are generator parameters rather than layout features; no option row or count field can carry them, and the prompt states no actual numbers, so they are recorded here for the pipeline.
layout_placement is empty: every pick here is drawn geometry, and the prompt asked for no invisible volumes, markers or triggers.

would have asked: Sounds like a shared open-world vehicle map — one common city everyone drives around, a grid of vehicle-width asphalt streets with intersections, and dense blocks of varying-height buildings between them. I'd add the sidewalks, lane markings and crosswalks, street lights, roadside trees and parking lots you listed on top. That's the standard single-pass build with no slow steps. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: no shape question was needed — "a grid layout of streets" already answers it. I would only have confirmed that cars actually drive these streets rather than the city being a static diorama, since that is what keeps traversal and reachability checks in the build instead of routing it as a SET.
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space? — traffic and pedestrians, or a distinct downtown landmark, would be the obvious additions and neither was assumed here.
